proposals.title: Context Composition Can Reverse Do-PFN's Uplift Ranking: A Case Study on Criteo
proposals.one_sentence_thesis: On Criteo, Do-PFN ranks uplift in reverse when its in-context examples keep the natural (≈4–5%) outcome rate, and balancing outcomes within each treatment arm of the context makes its ranking positive on a frozen 2.09M-row holdout (Qini −0.046 → +0.048); among the three foundation models tested this effect is specific to Do-PFN, it is associated with the sign of the score's rank correlation with estimated baseline risk, it is non-monotone in the outcome share, and the best composition tried does not beat HistGB learners trained on 2M rows.

rqs.rq: RQ1. In cross-validation, does the outcome composition of the context change the sign of a causal foundation model's uplift ranking, and is the effect specific to one model?
rqs.answer: On Criteo (4.8% visit rate), Do-PFN ranks users in reverse under random (R) and treatment-balanced (T) contexts at every context size from 512 to 4,096 (K=1024: Qini −0.074 and −0.077), and balancing outcomes within each arm (T+Y) makes the ranking positive (K=1024 gain +0.133, fold-level 95% CI [0.102, 0.165]). The gain is specific to Do-PFN: CausalPFN and TabPFN-T show no detectable change (+0.006 and −0.010, intervals spanning about ±0.1), classical learners fitted on the same 1,024 context rows are not inverted, and LZD (3.4%) shows the same signs only within run-to-run noise.

K=1024 (15 runs = 5 folds × 3 context seeds): R 0/15 and T 1/15 runs positive (fold t(4) −8.7 and −6.3); T+Y−T positive in 15/15 runs and 5/5 folds, +0.133 [0.102, 0.165]. The inversion rests on one strong dataset: LZD is within noise, T+Y also helps Do-PFN on Hillstrom (where nothing is inverted) and hurts it on RetailHero, and on Orange (non-randomized) the CV-selected Do-PFN configuration is negative on the holdout in all three seeds (−0.010). rqs.rq: RQ2. Does the T+Y repair hold on a frozen holdout, and how wrong are Do-PFN's effect estimates under treatment-balanced contexts?
rqs.answer: On the full frozen Criteo holdout (2,093,918 rows; T+Y selected on CV and frozen before the holdout), Do-PFN's Qini rises from −0.046 (T) to +0.048 (T+Y), a gain of +0.094 with three-seed t-interval [0.037, 0.150] (AUUC also positive), but the uplift@10% interval [−1.3, +4.9] pp includes zero. Under T the predicted effects have the wrong sign for most users (median −0.17 to −0.40 pp; 94–97% of predictions negative) against an observed treated-minus-control difference of +1.01 pp, whereas under T+Y the medians are positive (+0.36 to +0.96 pp).

proposals.title: When an In-Context Causal Model Ranks Uplift Backwards: Detecting and Repairing Context-Composition Failures of Do-PFN
proposals.one_sentence_thesis: With a 1024-row context, Do-PFN ranks Criteo users in reverse when the context is random or treatment-balanced. On Criteo this failure shows up without uplift labels as scores anti-correlated with baseline risk, and enriching each arm of the context with positive outcomes repairs it (full-holdout Qini -0.046 to +0.048 with T+Y; 0.075 with a 20% outcome share on a 200k-row subsample). The repaired model is not distinguishable from HistGB learners trained on 2M rows, while CausalPFN and TabPFN-T neither fail this way nor benefit from the repair.

rqs.rq: RQ1 (failure). When does context composition make an in-context causal model rank uplift in reverse?
rqs.answer: Only Do-PFN fails, and robustly only on Criteo (visit rate 4.8%): with random or treatment-balanced contexts its CV Qini is negative at every K from 512 to 4096 (K=1024: -0.074 and -0.077, 0/15 and 1/15 runs positive), and on the full holdout T contexts give Qini -0.046 (3/3 seeds) with effects of the wrong sign (median predicted CATE -0.2 to -0.4 pp, 94-97% of rows negative, against an observed ATE of +1.01 pp). LZD (3.4%) shows the same signs only within run-to-run noise (p = 0.15-0.24), Hillstrom, RetailHero and Orange show no consistent inversion, and CausalPFN and TabPFN-T are not inverted on any dataset (all R/T cell means >= -0.010).

proposals.title: The Context Sets the Sign: Outcome Composition and Inverted Uplift Rankings in Do-PFN
proposals.one_sentence_thesis: In Do-PFN, the share of positive outcomes in a fixed-size context, not the context size, decides whether uplift is ranked forwards or backwards on Criteo: natural and treatment-balanced contexts give negative Qini with scores anti-aligned to estimated baseline risk, outcome-balanced contexts give positive Qini on a frozen 2.09M-row holdout, and CausalPFN, TabPFN-T and classical learners fitted on the same rows do not invert.

rqs.rq: RQ1. Does the outcome composition of a fixed-size context, rather than its size, decide the sign of Do-PFN's uplift ranking?
rqs.answer: Yes on Criteo (visit rate 4.8%): with random or treatment-balanced contexts Do-PFN's CV Qini is negative at every K from 512 to 4096 (-0.072 to -0.085; 14-15 of 15 runs negative per cell), and with treatment-balanced contexts on the frozen 2.09M-row holdout it predicts a negative effect for 94-97% of users against an observed treated-minus-control difference of +1.01 pp, whereas balancing outcomes within each arm (T+Y) makes CV Qini positive at every K (gain +0.130 averaged over K; 5/5 folds, fold t-interval [0.104, 0.157]). LZD (3.4%) shows the same signs only in cell means and within run-to-run noise, and Hillstrom, RetailHero and Orange show no consistent inversion in CV.

Clearest practitioner arc (failure, detection, repair, comparison). RQ1 and RQ4 are well backed, but the claims that set this proposal apart overreach. (1) RQ2 says 'This reverses the ranking because observed uplift sits in the top two risk deciles'. All verifiers reject this kind of mechanism claim: mu0 comes from one fitted model, rho is about 0 at T+Y while Qini is +0.056, LZD Spearman is 0.10, and H4 never got the interval its own protocol requires. (2) 'A check that needs no uplift labels flags it' is a post hoc diagnostic. By the proposal's own counts, 22 of 67 runs with negative rho are not inverted (at the 35% share rho < 0 in 15/15 runs while Qini > 0 in 12/15), yet the RQ is marked closed_with_caveat. (3) The thesis and RQ3 say 'enriching each arm with positive outcomes repairs it', which the 10% share (CV -0.051, 0/5 folds) and the 35% share (holdout -0.007) contradict. (5) 'Validation should average several context draws' is advice that was never tested. Its run counts and LZD 0.10 recheck correctly. The 20% median-CATE and negative-share figures remain unverified. final_rq_list.rq: RQ1. In cross-validation, does the outcome composition of a fixed-size context change the sign of Do-PFN's uplift ranking, and is the inversion a property of the context rows or of the model that reads them?
final_rq_list.answer: On Criteo (4.8% visit rate), Do-PFN's CV Qini is negative under random and treatment-balanced contexts at every K from 512 to 4,096 and turns positive when outcomes are balanced within each arm (K=1024: T -0.077, T+Y +0.056; gain +0.133, fold-level 95% CI [0.102, 0.165], 5/5 folds), while CausalPFN, TabPFN-T and logistic/HistGB learners fitted on the same 1,024 rows are not inverted and Do-PFN's T+Y gain exceeds the other two foundation models' gains by +0.13 [0.04, 0.21] and +0.14 [0.06, 0.22], so the inversion is specific to Do-PFN on these contexts; LZD (3.4%) shows the same signs only within run-to-run noise, and Hillstrom, RetailHero and Orange show no consistent inversion in CV.
final_rq_list.status: closed_with_caveat: covers CV only, one robust dataset and K <= 4,096. The 15 runs are 5 folds x 3 context seeds, so lead with fold-level (df = 4) tests, and write the fold intervals and the interaction into a project script over mechanism_runs.csv (CPU, seconds). Call the classical controls 'not inverted', not 'positive' (+0.005 to +0.025, not distinguishable from zero). A second rare-outcome holdout would need DataSphere GPU time (the local GPU has been released) and is not realistic before Nov 17, so scope the title and claims to Do-PFN on Criteo.

final_rq_list.rq: RQ2. Does the CV-selected T+Y repair hold on the frozen Criteo holdout, and how wrong are Do-PFN's effect signs under treatment-balanced contexts?
final_rq_list.answer: On the 2,093,918-row Criteo holdout (contrast chosen on CV and frozen before the holdout; three context seeds), Do-PFN's Qini rises from -0.046 with T to +0.048 with T+Y (gain +0.094, three-seed t-interval [0.037, 0.150]; AUUC [0.015, 0.059]; uplift@10% [-1.3, +4.9] pp, so not established), and with T contexts 94-97% of predicted effects are negative (median -0.17 to -0.40 pp) although the observed treated-minus-control visit difference is +1.01 pp (SE 0.04).
final_rq_list.status: closed_with_caveat: Qini and AUUC are closed, but they are near-collinear and not independent evidence; uplift@10% stays open. Label the [0.085, 0.102] cluster bootstrap as conditional on the three contexts: the between-seed SD of the gain is 0.023, against about 0.005 within a seed. Never write 'pre-specified'. Disclose that the holdout was used before (48 frozen runs and the CV-probe reference fit). Argue only the sign error: the T+Y context ATE is zero by construction, and the T-context mean and SD come from the 1.3-2.4% of predictions outside [-1, 1]. Any further context seeds would run on DataSphere.

final_rq_list.rq: RQ3. Is the sign of Do-PFN's ranking associated with the sign of its scores' rank correlation with estimated baseline risk, and does the non-monotone response to the outcome share replicate on the holdout?

scores.comments: This is the proposal most faithful to the verifier fixes. Each answer states its own counterexamples (rho near 0 at T+Y, LZD within noise, 'only partly' for share tuning), and every interval leads with a fold-level or three-seed t-interval. Its remark that T+Y contexts have a context ATE of exactly zero by construction is right (CPU check: 256 rows in every (t, y) cell). For WSDM it reads as a defensive audit. The headline effect is split between RQ1 (CV) and RQ2 (holdout). RQ1 and RQ4 each bundle four or five sub-claims (model specificity, controls, LZD; share tuning, LZD transfer, the HistGB comparison, CV-selection fragility), so the answers run to paragraphs. The 'case study' title hides the model-specific, non-monotone sign flip, and the proposal never positions the work against outcome undersampling in rare-outcome uplift.

This has the clearest arc for a WSDM practitioner audience (failure, detection, repair, comparison), and RQ1, RQ3 and RQ4 are well supported. Its self-flagged 20% numbers hold: recomputed on CPU from the share NPZs, the median predicted CATE is -0.06/-0.10/-0.06 pp, 73/58/74% of predictions are negative, and the mean is +6.1 to +7.3 pp. The thesis and RQ2, however, present a label-free detector that the data do not support. On Criteo, 22 of the 67 CV runs with negative rho have positive Qini (at the 35% share rho < 0 in 15/15 runs, yet Qini > 0 in 12/15), and rho is near 0 at T+Y while Qini is positive. The pooled Qini-rho Spearman of 0.83 comes almost entirely from differences between shares: within a share it is 0.17, and at 20% it is -0.03, so rho cannot pick good context draws. On LZD the Spearman is 0.10, and rho > 0 in 15/15 runs at 10% and at 20% while mean Qini is negative. The one regularity, that no Criteo fold cell with rho > 0 has negative Qini (0/14), is one-sided and was found post hoc, and the protocol's H4 interval was never computed. RQ2 also folds in a separate point about labelled validation. Finally, 'not inverted on any dataset' for CausalPFN/TabPFN-T invites a reviewer to point at Orange, where all 8 TabPFN-T R/T cells are slightly negative.

This proposal best combines a sharp, WSDM-relevant claim with the evidence. Each RQ asks one thing. RQ2 ('rows or model?') is the question reviewers will ask, and it is answered with the interaction test and the budget-matched controls. The share axis gives one coherent main figure. It is the only proposal that positions the work against outcome undersampling for rare-outcome uplift and flags that Do-PFN is documented for continuous outcomes. The details the verifiers did not cover check out on CPU: the T contexts hold 21/24, 17/26 and 24/19 visits per arm, and holdout_share_contrasts.csv gives 20% - T +0.128 [0.093, 0.162] and T+Y - T +0.103 [0.041, 0.165]. Fixes needed: (1) the headline full-holdout T vs T+Y confirmation sits in RQ4 rather than RQ1, and RQ4 asks two questions; (2) RQ3's one-sentence answer leaves its counterexamples (rho near 0 at T+Y; negative at 35% in CV while Qini is positive; LZD) to the evidence block, and it says Qini 'tracks' rho on the strength of the pooled 0.83, which is between-share (within-share 0.17); (3) 'not the context size' holds only for K 512-4,096; (4) the McDowell et al. final_rq_list.rq: RQ1. Does the outcome composition of a fixed-size context, rather than its size, decide the sign of Do-PFN's uplift ranking, and does the outcome-balanced repair hold on a frozen holdout?
final_rq_list.answer: On Criteo (4.8% visit rate), yes: with random or treatment-balanced contexts Do-PFN's CV Qini is negative at every context size from 512 to 4,096 rows (-0.072 to -0.085), balancing outcomes within each treatment arm (T+Y) makes it positive at every size (gain +0.13 averaged over sizes, 5/5 folds, fold t-interval [0.104, 0.157]), and on the frozen 2.09M-row holdout T+Y lifts Qini from -0.046 to +0.048 (+0.094, t-interval over three context draws [0.037, 0.150]; uplift@10% unresolved at [-1.3, +4.9] pp), whereas LZD (3.4%) shows the same signs only within fold noise and Hillstrom, RetailHero and Orange show no consistent inversion.
final_rq_list.status: closed_with_caveat: Criteo is the only robust dataset. With three context draws per arm, the top-decile metric is unresolved. LZD has no R/T holdout run, and context sizes were tested only up to 4,096.

final_rq_list.rq: RQ2. Is the inversion a property of the context rows or of the model that reads them?
final_rq_list.answer: Of the model: on the same Criteo contexts, T+Y gives CausalPFN and TabPFN-T no detectable gain (at K=1,024 Do-PFN's gain exceeds theirs by +0.13 [0.04, 0.21] and +0.14 [0.06, 0.22]), neither model is inverted (R/T Qini +0.007 to +0.077 in all 16 Criteo cells), and logistic and HistGB learners fitted on the same 1,024 rows are not inverted (mean Qini +0.005 to +0.025, not distinguishable from zero) and beat Do-PFN in 12-14 of 15 paired runs.
final_rq_list.status: closed_with_caveat: CV only and Criteo only; the LZD interaction is not significant. The controls are noisy (run SD 0.07-0.09), so 'not inverted' rests on paired comparisons and fold-level tests. Why only Do-PFN inverts has not been tested. The fold-level interaction test still has to move from scratch output into a project script (CPU).

final_rq_list.rq: RQ3. Is the sign of Do-PFN's ranking associated with how its scores align with baseline risk?
final_rq_list.answer: On Criteo, as an association only: every configuration with negative mean Qini (R, T and 10% in CV; T and 35% on the holdout) has scores negatively rank-correlated with estimated baseline risk mu0 in every run and seed, the best share (20%) is positively correlated in all 15 CV runs and all 3 holdout seeds, and observed uplift sits in the top two mu0 deciles (2.4 and 4.3 pp vs about 0 in deciles 1-7), but the correlation is near zero at T+Y and negative at 35% in CV while Qini is positive, and it does not track Qini on LZD (Spearman 0.10), so it is neither a demonstrated mechanism nor a validated label-free detector.
final_rq_list.status: closed_with_caveat as an association; open as a mechanism. The pooled Qini-rho Spearman (0.83) comes from differences between shares (0.17 within a share), so do not quote it as run-level tracking. Still to do on CPU (minutes): the holdout rho interval that the protocol's own H4 rule requires, and the mu0-decile table, both as project scripts. A mechanism would need Do-PFN's per-arm predictions under T and T+Y on the CV eval rows, which means GPU time on DataSphere because the local GPU is released.

final_rq_list.rq: RQ4. Can the outcome share be tuned on cross-validation into a reliable, competitive ranker?
final_rq_list.answer: Only partly: the share response is non-monotone (35% falls below both 20% and T+Y in CV and in every holdout seed; holdout 35% - 20% = -0.082, t-interval [-0.107, -0.058]); the CV-chosen 20% share beats T+Y in all three holdout seeds (uplift@10% +1.80 pp, t [0.41, 3.18]) but its Qini edge is within context-to-context variation (+0.024, t [-0.003, 0.052]) and does not transfer to LZD (CV 20% - T+Y = -0.026); and at Qini 0.075 it stays slightly below, though not distinguishable from, HistGB S- and T-learners trained on 2M development rows (0.082, 0.079), with point predictions usable only for ranking (mean +6.1 to +7.3 pp, median -0.06 to -0.10 pp, against an observed +1.01 pp).
final_rq_list.status: partial: a positive claim that 20% beats T+Y needs about 7 more context seeds per arm on the fixed 200k rows, with T+Y re-scored there for strict pairing, and a two-level (contexts x rows) interval; these runs go to DataSphere, not the released local GPU. The reference-learner interval (S - 20% = +0.007 [-0.006, +0.020], conditional on the contexts) exists only in verifier scratch output and needs a project script (CPU). The 20% share was picked from six shares on Criteo CV at K=1024 only.
